title: The tour that really left that month
subtopic: T5 — the professional's answer, in the same autumn
learning_goal: Know that the first commercial round-the-world tour left in the same month and took 222 days, so eighty was a provocation rather than a schedule.

narration.script: While Verne was inventing this, a travel agent was actually doing it. In late September eighteen seventy-two — days before Fogg's fictional departure — Thomas Cook led eight paying customers out of Liverpool on the first round-the-world tour ever sold. It cost two hundred guineas. It took two hundred and twenty-two days. So the real answer, from the man whose job this was, in the actual month: about seven months. Eighty days was not a schedule. It was a provocation.
